comparison_intro: Reproduce earlier-row values only where each SAS LAG occurrence executes on every row. Preserve missing history and the original sequence.

language_notes.sas: Macro transform supplies source/result names. Each LAG occurrence maintains a separate queue initialized with missing values.
language_notes.python: Series.shift with no frequency moves values by row. Out is a copy; arithmetic preserves unavailable history as missing.
language_notes.r: lag_rows pads with NA and clamps the lag for short vectors. stats::lag changes time-series attributes and is not this row-shift operation.

semantic_notes.title: Missing means no prior observation
semantic_notes.text: Do not fill the first prior value with zero: that manufactures a change of 10. Keep the two missing starting positions of the two-row lag.

semantic_notes.title: Respect call history
semantic_notes.text: Conditional SAS LAG calls advance their queue only when executed. Such a program requires separate analysis; unconditional shifts are insufficient.

tests.name: Original known-answer fixture
tests.catches: Wrong lag direction, wraparound, missing-to-zero fills or reordered predecessors.

tests.name: Added one-row data set
tests.expected: Both previous-value columns and change are missing; one row remains.
tests.catches: Lag padding longer than input, zero filling, wraparound and invalid short-vector indexing.

tests.name: Preserve order, types and missing
tests.input: Original rows with non-default Python/R labels; nullable Python numeric values.
tests.expected: Input unchanged; id/value order preserved; numeric results and exact missing masks.
tests.catches: Input mutation, row sorting/dropping, text outputs or missing-position drift.

scope: Only the supplied per-row SAS LAG and LAG2 calls. A singleton is an added local boundary test. Conditional calls, retained targets and automatic resets at BY boundaries need separate analysis.
